documents.source_category: Interim Financial Statements for the Quarter ended 30th June 2026

financials_interim.notes: LOLC Finance PLC (LOFC) is a licensed finance company (NBFI); this filing has a SINGLE set of financial statements (no separate Group/Company columns -- the entity does not consolidate any subsidiaries in this report), so basis is recorded as GROUP by convention (same figures would apply to a COMPANY row, so no separate COMPANY row is entered to avoid a duplicate). Per this project's NBFI mapping convention: revenue = Interest income (22,917,498,522), cost_of_sales = Interest expense (9,551,572,052), gross_profit = Net interest income (13,365,926,470) -- NOT 'Total operating income' (Rs.14,018,519,599), because using Total Operating Income as revenue would double-count interest expense (already netted out to get there) if cost_of_sales/finance_costs were also populated. Between gross_profit and operating_profit the filing has further layers not captured by single schema fields (net fee income +733.7m, net trading losses -179.1m, other operating income -81.1m, impairment charge -234.8m, personnel/depreciation/other opex -6,939.9m) -- operating_profit is therefore the filing's own 'Profit before tax expense' subtotal (6,843,890,184), not a gross_profit-minus-cost_of_sales derivation. The filing presents only ONE tax-type line -- 'Taxes on financial services' (1,442,926,205) -- between 'Profit before tax expense' and 'Profit for the period', with no separate VAT-on-Financial-Services/SSCL split from income tax; consequently profit_before_tax is set equal to operating_profit (6,843,890,184) and tax_expense = 1,442,926,205, which ties exactly to disclosed PAT (6,843,890,184-1,442,926,205=5,400,963,979). current_assets/current_liabilities/inventory/trade_receivables are left blank per the NBFI convention (no current/non-current split is presented on the SOFP, and the loan book -- Financial assets at amortised cost, loans and advances to customers, Rs.429,788,469,802 -- is NOT a trade receivable). short_term_borrowings = Bank overdraft only (6,565,502,179, unambiguously short-term); long_term_borrowings = 'Financial liabilities at amortised cost - borrowings' (105,045,192,133) -- this filing does NOT disclose a maturity split for this borrowings line, so classifying the whole balance as long-term is an approximation, made because the disclosed listed debentures within it (Types A/B/C) carry 5-year tenors; customer deposits (Rs.288,830,379,883, 'due to depositors') are deliberately EXCLUDED from both borrowings fields per instruction -- they are funding liabilities, not debt facilities.

interim_updates.note_text: LOLC Finance PLC (LOFC), Sri Lanka's largest licensed finance company, reported Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026) profit after tax of Rs.5.40bn, up a modest 3.8% YoY from Rs.5.20bn -- much slower than the 30.5% growth in interest income (Rs.22.92bn vs Rs.17.56bn), for two specific reasons. First, funding costs rose faster than lending income: interest expense jumped 56.5% to Rs.9.55bn as customer deposits (Rs.288.83bn, +6% since 31 March 2026) and borrowings (Rs.105.05bn, +7% since 31 March 2026) both grew to fund the Rs.437.75bn gross loan book (+3.5% since 31 March 2026); net interest income still grew a healthy 16.7% to Rs.13.37bn. Second, and more directly, Net gains/(losses) from trading flipped from a Rs.281.9m GAIN in Q1 FY2025/26 to a Rs.179.1m LOSS this quarter -- a Rs.461m negative swing that shows up entirely in the Eliminations/Unallocated segment column (segment PBT of -Rs.135.8m in 2026 vs +Rs.136.0m in 2025) and by itself explains most of the gap between core operating momentum and headline profit growth. At the lending-segment level, Gold Loans PBT surged 133.8% YoY to Rs.1,030.6m (from Rs.440.9m) as the gold loan book grew to Rs.76.25bn from Rs.70.24bn at 31 March 2026, and Personal Finance PBT grew 26.4% to Rs.1,272.9m, while SME Finance -- still the largest segment by assets at Rs.260.5bn -- saw PBT fall 6.9% to Rs.3,615.6m from Rs.3,885.5m. Operating expenses grew 18.8% to Rs.6.94bn (personnel costs +33%, depreciation & amortisation +63% to Rs.666.0m) and the net impairment charge rose to Rs.234.8m from Rs.180.1m -- both consistent with continued branch network growth (205 branches, up from 201 a year ago) rather than credit deterioration, since the Net Non-Performing Loan ratio actually improved to 3.63% from 5.49% a year ago. The filing presents a single combined tax line, 'Taxes on financial services' (Rs.1.44bn), between PBT and PAT with no separate income-tax/VAT-FS split disclosed.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one has been collected for LOFC -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. Additionally, LOLC Finance PLC's Statement of Financial Position in this filing discloses only a 30.06.2026 (unaudited) vs 31.03.2026 (audited) comparison -- it does NOT provide a 30.06.2025 balance-sheet comparative (standard LKAS 34 practice: SOFP compares to the prior audited year-end, not the prior-year interim date). Consequently the yoy_json above is built entirely from Income Statement / Cash Flow Statement lines (which DO carry genuine 30.06.2025 comparatives); no YoY comparison is offered for balance-sheet items (total assets, equity, loan book, deposits, borrowings) since no true year-ago balance-sheet figure exists in this document. The short_term_borrowings/long_term_borrowings split (bank overdraft vs the Rs.105.05bn 'borrowings' line) is an estimate as explained in the financial_statements 'notes' field, since the filing gives no maturity breakdown of that line.
interim_updates.takeaway: PAT grew a modest 3.8% YoY -- far slower than the 30%+ growth in interest income -- mainly because of a Rs.461m negative swing in trading results (from a Rs.282m gain to a Rs.179m loss) plus a 56.5% jump in interest expense; underlying lending momentum was considerably stronger than the headline PAT growth suggests, particularly in Gold Loans (segment PBT +133.8% YoY), while SME Finance (the largest segment) saw profit contract 6.9%.
operational_highlights: Gross loan book grew 3.5% since 31 March 2026 to Rs.437.75bn, across SME, Personal Finance, Alternate Finance and Gold Loan products
Net interest income +16.7% YoY to Rs.13.37bn as interest income (+30.5% to Rs.22.92bn) outpaced the absolute rise in interest expense (+56.5% to Rs.9.55bn)
Customer deposits grew 6% since 31 March 2026 to Rs.288.83bn and borrowings grew 7% to Rs.105.05bn to fund asset growth
Total equity strengthened to Rs.160.81bn from Rs.155.40bn at 31 March 2026, lifting Net Asset Value per share to Rs.5.44 from Rs.5.26

Tier 1 and Total Capital Adequacy Ratios of 22.43% and 22.21% remain well above the 10%/17% regulatory minimums, though both eased from 24.96%/24.71% a year earlier as the balance sheet grew faster than capital

Board approved (post period-end, 22 July 2026) a share repurchase of up to 2.30bn shares (7.8% of shares in issue) at Rs.7.00/share for up to Rs.16.09bn -- a subsequent event not reflected in the 30 June 2026 balance sheet
key_drivers: Net gains/(losses) from trading swung from +Rs.281.9m to -Rs.179.1m, a Rs.461m negative swing recorded in the Eliminations/Unallocated segment -- the single largest drag on YoY profit growth
Gold Loans segment PBT +133.8% YoY (Rs.440.9m to Rs.1,030.6m) on a gold loan book that grew to Rs.76.25bn from Rs.70.24bn at 31 March 2026 -- the largest positive segment-level driver
SME Finance segment PBT -6.9% YoY (Rs.3,885.5m to Rs.3,615.6m) despite being the largest segment by assets (Rs.260.5bn) -- the largest negative segment-level driver
Interest expense +56.5% YoY (Rs.6.10bn to Rs.9.55bn) as deposit and borrowing balances grew to fund lending -- compresses margin even as absolute net interest income still rose
